item.title: 'It will end pretty soon': Trump hints at sooner resolution to US-Iran war
item.description: Expressing confidence, US President Trump suggested that the Iran conflict is nearing its end, arguing that Tehran cannot bear its continuation. He remains hopeful about negotiations related to the Strait of Hormuz. The US is resolute in preventing Iran from developing nuclear weapons. Meanwhile, Iran's defence minister asserts that their military is on standby for any potential threats, and the parliament speaker claims that the US.
item.dc:creator: VIJAYA SRIVASTAVA

item.title: UPI charges: Lok Sabha passes bill for government to make changes
item.description: The Lok Sabha has taken a vital step by passing a bill aimed at simplifying tax rules to enhance investment attractiveness. The new legislation abolishes a limitation on specific electronic payment options, allowing banks and providers to charge merchants on transactions. Additionally, the government is empowered to revise the zero-MDR scheme for UPI and RuPay. This initiative is poised to drive advancements in the financial sector’s infrastructure and innovative capabilities.
item.dc:creator: TNN

item.title: SC dismisses plea challenging Delhi HC relief to Hinduja brothers in Bofors case
item.description: The Supreme Court has officially closed the chapter on the Bofors payoff case by dismissing an appeal that challenged the Delhi High Court's 2005 ruling, which had previously annulled criminal proceedings against the Hinduja brothers. Advocate Ajay K Agrawal filed the appeal, but the court decided against allowing more time for arguments, finalizing the legal dispute once and for all.
item.dc:creator: VIJAYA SRIVASTAVA

item.title: Rahane snubs MS Dhoni, Virat Kohli; names India's greatest-ever cricketer
item.description: Ajinkya Rahane recently retired from all cricket formats. He named Sachin Tendulkar as India's greatest-ever cricketer. Tendulkar had a remarkable 24-year international career for India. Rahane played alongside Tendulkar in domestic and IPL matches. He also captained India in all three formats.
item.dc:creator: TOI SPORTS DESK

item.title: Netanyahu calls PM Modi, discusses bilateral ties, West Asia situation
item.description: In a significant phone discussion, Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu evaluated the progress made in their strategic partnership and bilateral engagements. They also addressed current developments in West Asia, amidst Israel's increasing international scrutiny due to its military actions. This exchange highlights their continued efforts to bolster cooperation and deepen ties between India and Israel.
item.dc:creator: TNN

item.title: Kentucky family rejects $26M offer for farm land over ‘poison’ data center
item.description: A Kentucky family has taken a stand against a tempting $26 million proposal for their farmland, which an undisclosed company intended for a grand AI data center. The family champions the importance of preserving agricultural land and food security, emphasizing that their attachment to the property goes beyond mere monetary value. In contrast, other local landowners appear to be more receptive to selling.
item.dc:creator: TOI TECH DESK

item.title: Bombay high court overturns Tejpal acquittal, awards 10-year jail term
item.description: HC Tears Through Trial Court’s Judgement
item.dc:creator: TOI

item.title: Sonam Wangchuk says Rahul Gandhi ignored his offer to end his fast
item.description: Sonam Wangchuk voiced disappointment with political leaders after his hunger strike concluded. His wife Gitanjali sought Rahul Gandhi's involvement but received no positive response. Union ministers also reportedly broke a promise regarding the release of photos. Wangchuk felt leaders showed a narrow approach and arrived late to his protest. He praised the apolitical CJP organization for its fair and just advocacy.
item.dc:creator: TNN

item.title: Kharge-Rijiju face-off in Rajya Sabha; opposition stalls House over Amit Shah
item.description: The Rajya Sabha approved the Appropriation Bill, 2026, authorizing fund withdrawals for excess expenditure. Opposition members repeatedly demanded Home Minister Amit Shah's presence in the House. Parliamentary affairs minister Kiren Rijiju was asked to convey their sentiments to Shah. Leader of the Opposition Mallikarjun Kharge sought the Home Minister's statement on student police action. The opposition also requested the Prime Minister's apology for the alleged police excesses.
item.dc:creator: TNN

item.title: Priscilla Chan founded a school in 2016; 10 yrs later, it closed after $125m funding
item.description: The Primary School, a tuition-free institution, will close in June after a decade of operation. This school provided education, healthcare, and family support to low-income children. The Chan Zuckerberg Initiative will not continue funding beyond the upcoming academic year. Academic results remained below state averages, prompting the board's decision. The initiative pledged fifty million dollars to aid the transition for affected students.
item.dc:creator: TOI TECH DESK

item.dc:creator: CHIDANAND RAJGHATTA

item.title: Popeyes sued for $1.5M over 'condom-like' object found in fried chicken
item.description: A Popeyes restaurant in Houston, Texas, is facing a lawsuit after two customers alleged they found a "condom-like foreign object" embedded inside a piece of fried chicken during what was supposed to be a routine family meal. Plaintiffs Justin Howard and Danielle McKinnon claim they continue to suffer physical discomfort, emotional distress and mental anguish following the incident.
item.dc:creator: TOI WORLD DESK

item.title: 97-year-old Betty Bromage breaks own record as oldest female wing walker
item.description: At 97, Betty Bromage has broken her own Guinness World Record as the oldest female wing walker. The Cheltenham resident completed the daring challenge to raise funds for the stroke unit at Cheltenham General Hospital, where she was treated after suffering a stroke in 2025, proving resilience knows no age.
item.dc:creator: TOI WORLD DESK

item.title: After 'ban' on Claude Code, Microsoft has more 'bad news' for Anthropic
item.description: Microsoft has told engineers that "tokenmaxxing is not what we are optimizing for" in a new internal memo from EVP Jay Parikh. The memo makes OpenAI's GPT-5.6 the default internal model, replacing an auto-router that had been sending GitHub Copilot workloads to Anthropic's Claude. Every Microsoft division now carries an AI token budget target, months after Claude Code licences were cancelled.
item.dc:creator: TOI TECH DESK

item.title: ‘Michael 2’ under way, film makers to start shooting by 2026 end
item.description: Filming for the Michael Jackson biopic sequel is slated to begin by year's end. The production company aims for a potential 2027 release date for the film. This sequel follows the significant worldwide success of the first movie. Some omitted elements from the initial film may appear in the new installment. The company reported overall financial gains due to recent film successes.
item.dc:creator: TOI ENTERTAINMENT DESK

item.title: Jana Nayagan day 15: Thalapathy Vijay film grosses Rs 308.67 crore worldwide
item.description: Jana Nayagan's box office collections saw a decline on its fifteenth day. The film has now surpassed Rs 300 crore in worldwide gross collections. Its India net collection reached Rs 185.15 crore after fifteen days. Tamil Nadu remained the strongest market, contributing significantly to daily earnings. The movie's performance reflects Vijay's enduring star power.
item.dc:creator: TOI ENTERTAINMENT DESK

item.title: Congress MPs urge leadership to seek SP alliance talks ahead of UP polls
item.description: Uttar Pradesh Congress MPs are actively pushing for a partnership with the Samajwadi Party, considering it vital to mount a formidable challenge to the BJP in the upcoming elections. With a strong consensus among the MPs for quick action, party leaders are currently assessing viable constituencies and gathering data to facilitate negotiations, striving to strengthen their united front against the BJP's dominance in the state.
item.dc:creator: SUBODH GHILDIYAL

item.title: Can't exclude SC/ST creamy layer from quotas: Government to Supreme Court
item.description: The government is against extending the creamy layer to SC and ST reservation benefits, emphasizing that the challenges these communities face are rooted in more than economic issues. Reservation serves to right historical wrongs and ensure equitable access. The Supreme Court has permitted states to categorize castes within SC groups, but only Parliament holds the power to amend the lists of SC and ST populations eligible for these allocations.
item.dc:creator: DHANANJAY MAHAPATRA

item.title: Rahul reaches out to Gen Z through Instagram, backs student protest in Jharkhand
item.description: Rahul Gandhi took to Instagram to voice his support for student protests, labeling the education system as deeply flawed and in need of urgent reform. His remarks were made following a meeting with NEET protesters who detailed their encounters with police brutality. The students bravely shared stories of discrimination they faced while advocating for their rights.
item.dc:creator: SUBODH GHILDIYAL

item.title: Opposition opposes FCRA bill, says minorities being targeted
item.description: Rahul Gandhi briefed opposition parties on discussions regarding the delimitation bill. The opposition maintains its stand on women's reservation within the current Lok Sabha strength. Discussions also covered the FCRA bill, with concerns raised about its impact on minorities. Some members noted potential government removal of retrospective effect clauses. Parliamentary functioning remains contingent on government statements regarding protests and donations.
item.dc:creator: TNN

item.title: BJP to Congress: Let House function, Amit Shah will come
item.description: The BJP has called out Congress leaders Rahul Gandhi and Mallikarjun Kharge for allegedly spreading misinformation. They assert that Home Minister Shah is present at Parliament House, but is unable to participate due to ongoing protests. Continued disruptions by the opposition hinder legislative work, yet Shah is ready to address their concerns directly. The BJP confirmed Shah is in his office daily, awaiting the resumption of parliamentary activities.
item.dc:creator: TNN

item.title: Land-grab case: Supeme Court grants interim bail to Abhishek's PA
item.description: In a significant move, the Supreme Court has granted interim bail for one week to Sumit Roy, who serves as the personal assistant to TMC general secretary Abhishek Banerjee. Roy is implicated in the Salboni land-grabbing case, which followed the arrest of former TMC MLA Sujoy Hazra. Notably, the court has stayed Roy's arrest until it reconvenes for the next hearing.
item.dc:creator: TNN

item.title: 3 rebel TMC MPs to meet Prime Minister over breakfast
item.description: A trio of dissenting Trinamool MPs is set to engage with Prime Minister Narendra Modi following their earlier discussions with Union Minister Amit Shah related to pressing concerns. Notably, these lawmakers have distanced themselves from two NDA meetings. Additionally, other NCPI representatives and Shiv Sena MPs are expected to join them for a breakfast meeting with the Prime Minister on Friday morning.
item.dc:creator: TNN

item.title: Priyanka Chopra joins Russell Crowe in Hollywood sci-fi action thriller 'Bluefly'
item.description: Priyanka Chopra Jonas has announced her next Hollywood venture, a sci-fi action thriller. She will star opposite Russell Crowe in the film titled 'Bluefly'. The movie's plot involves a deep Congo mission to recover a mysterious downed aircraft. This project marks another significant international role for the acclaimed Indian actress. 'Bluefly' is scheduled for production and release in the future.
item.dc:creator: TOI ENTERTAINMENT DESK

item.title: 15 Indian seafarers killed in West Asia and Black Sea conflicts: Regulator
item.description: Geopolitical conflicts in West Asia and the Black Sea have endangered Indian seafarers. Fifteen Indian seafarers have died and two remain missing in recent months. Drone and missile attacks have become rampant in the Black Sea region. Piracy off Somalia and Houthi threats have also resurfaced significantly. India's maritime regulator is enhancing safety measures and tracking seafarers' well-being.
item.dc:creator: TNN

item.title: Amid cyber threats, IT ministry asked to expedite hirings
item.description: The finance ministry has sanctioned more posts for CERT-In, yet the hiring remains underway. With rising cyber threats dominating discussions, a parliamentary committee is pressing for expedited recruitment. The IndiaAI Mission's fellowship program initially struggled to attract candidates. In response, MeitY is implementing outreach sessions and promotional campaigns to encourage more applicants. Additionally, final touches are being made to recruitment guidelines for several scientific roles ahead of future job advertisements.
item.dc:creator: AABHAS SHARMA

item.title: SC says compulsory retirement not punitive, upholds CISF officer’s removal
item.description: The Supreme Court clarified that compulsory retirement is not a punishment for diminished performance, but rather a necessary step to uphold the standards of efficiency and discipline required. The court dismissed a plea from a CISF officer who disputed his removal after his performance had notably dropped from 'Good' to 'Average'. It emphasized the importance of consistent high performance among personnel in disciplined forces.
item.dc:creator: AMIT ANAND CHOUDHARY

item.title: Sharif begins 3-day Saudi visit, pushes defence ties amid West Asia escalation
item.dc:creator: VIJAYA SRIVASTAVA

item.title: Wangchuk gives govt 1 month to drop cases, compensate for Leh protest firing
item.description: In a bold move, the Leh Apex Body has presented the Union government with a one-month ultimatum, calling for the withdrawal of allegations against protesters and support for the families affected by last year’s tragedies. The relatives of four deceased demonstrators are adamant about receiving justice and compensation. They have signaled potential protests if their requests are ignored, underscoring the urgent need for the Centre's attention to Ladakh's pressing concerns.
item.dc:creator: NASEER GANAI

item.title: Supreme Court happy with progress in talks in Sunjay Kapur case
item.description: In an effort to resolve a high-profile family dispute, members are actively engaging in mediation under the supervision of ex-CJI DY Chandrachud, following a Supreme Court directive. So far, six sessions have taken place, where the parties have agreed to continue discussions. They are pursuing a comprehensive settlement related to trust claims, with mediation scheduled to run until November 2.
item.dc:creator: TNN

item.title: 5.7 lakh people fined Rs 5.1 cr in 2025-26 for smoking in public
item.description: In India, over 570,000 individuals were fined for smoking in public spaces, accumulating penalties exceeding Rs 51 million under the COTPA legislation. Karnataka led the charge, issuing the most fines. Interestingly, several states recorded no violations or fines throughout the year. Enforcement primarily lies with state governments, highlighting the varying levels of adherence to the public smoking ban.
item.dc:creator: ANUJA JAISWAL

item.title: Railways rolls out National Permit-like license for container train operators
item.dc:creator: DIPAK K DASH

item.title: Nearly 200 deaths linked to weight-loss drugs Ozempic and Mounjaro in the UK
item.description: UK health authorities have recorded almost 200 fatalities linked to the anti-obesity medications Mounjaro and Wegovy. These drugs have been associated with more than 150,000 adverse effects. Notably, semaglutide, which is marketed as Ozempic and Wegovy, accounts for 59 deaths, while tirzepatide, known as Mounjaro, has resulted in 120 deaths and over 106,000 adverse reactions, and liraglutide, or Saxenda, has 37 deaths with 4,528 adverse effects recorded.
item.dc:creator: NAOMI CANTON

item.title: Foreign funding up despite tightening of FCRA rules
item.description: Despite the tightening of regulations, foreign contributions to NGOs have surged. Recently, however, there has been a notable decline in the number of registered NGOs, now totaling merely 14,500 compared to several lakh in the past. The government emphasizes that the amendments focus on specific foreign-funded channels, aiming to enhance oversight without hindering the broader civil society framework.
item.dc:creator: BHARTI JAIN

item.title: Amit Shah assured proposed FCRA changes will not be retrospective, says Mizoram CM
item.description: Chief minister Lalduhoma from Mizoram held a pivotal meeting with Home Minister Amit Shah on Thursday, where Shah confirmed that amendments to the FCRA will not have a retroactive effect. Church representatives were also part of the discussion, emphasizing the need for suggestions to safeguard the FCRA. A vital debate on the proposed bill is set for August 12, promising to clarify future legislative actions.
item.dc:creator: AMBIKA PANDIT AND KUMAR RAKESH

item.title: Is Zendaya pregnant? Truth behind the viral baby bump photo revealed
item.description: Zendaya's baby bump photo has gone viral across social media, leaving fans convinced that the actor is expecting her first child with Tom Holland. However, it looks like the viral image is fake and was created using artificial intelligence, with the original photograph dating back to 2023.
item.dc:creator: TOI ENTERTAINMENT DESK

item.title: Quote of the day by Larry Page: “You need to get one thing done well, or else…”
item.description: Larry Page advocates for completing one task well before starting others. This focused approach builds confidence and a strong foundation for future endeavors. Many fields, including education and business, benefit from this principle of deep mastery. Rushing tasks can create future problems, while high standards require patience and revision. This principle remains relevant amidst modern distractions and constant communication shifts.
item.dc:creator: TOI TECH DESK

item.title: Territorial Army’s contribution significant for govt’s 'Viksit Bharat' vision: Rajnath
item.description: Defence Minister Rajnath Singh praised the Territorial Army's significant contributions to Viksit Bharat. The force embodies the citizen-soldier concept, safeguarding borders and maintaining internal security. Territorial Army personnel provide surge capacity and act as a bridge to society. They are also first responders during natural calamities and aid environmental conservation efforts. Ecological task forces have planted ten crore saplings, supporting national climate goals.
item.dc:creator: SURENDRA SINGH

item.title: Gaganyaan makes progress as critical human-rating milestones achieved: Space min
item.description: India's Gaganyaan mission has achieved significant milestones in developing critical human-rating systems. Propulsion stages and structures for the launch vehicle have been fully developed and tested. Crew safety systems, including the escape system, have also been successfully developed and qualified. The first uncrewed experimental mission is targeted for late 2026. This will be followed by two more uncrewed flights before the maiden human orbital mission.
item.dc:creator: SURENDRA SINGH

item.title: Bengaluru company builds tech to keep ageing spacecraft alive
item.description: A Bengaluru-based startup is revolutionising space operations with its jetpack satellites designed to dock with aging spacecraft, effectively taking over propulsion responsibilities. Aule Space has successfully validated its crucial technology at an ISRO facility, setting the stage for future demonstrations. With plans for a groundbreaking private satellite docking trial next year, this innovation could save billions by prolonging the functionality of essential assets in orbit.
item.dc:creator: CHETHAN KUMAR

item.title: Hyderabad YouTuber Abhinav Reddy and German traveller Safira get engaged
item.description: A chance meeting between Indian YouTuber Abhinav Reddy, popularly known as Abhi Honey, and German traveller Safira during a trip to Bali has turned into a heartwarming cross-cultural love story that is now captivating millions on social media. What began as a casual friendship soon grew stronger, eventually leading Safira to invite Reddy to her childhood village in Germany.
item.dc:creator: TOI LIFESTYLE DESK

item.title: France submits detailed proposal to India’s request for 114 Rafales
item.description: France has made a formal proposal for supplying 114 Rafale fighter jets to India, estimating the deal at approximately Rs 3.25 lakh crore. This strategic partnership will see 94 jets produced locally under the Make-in-India initiative. The Indian government is now reviewing the proposal to ensure it aligns with the integration of indigenous missile systems, with hopes to finalize the agreement by the end of this year.
item.dc:creator: SURENDRA SINGH

item.title: Horoscope today: Daily astrological predictions for August 7, 2026
item.description: Horoscope Today: Read daily horoscope predictions for August 7, 2026. Know all about the astrological events and influences that will be affecting each of the 12 zodiac signs. Our astrologer has analyzed the movements of the planets and the alignment of the stars to bring you the most accurate and up-to-date horoscope predictions for the day ahead. Get ready to discover what the stars have in store for you today.

item.title: Newly elected PoK legislator is on police bail in UK for child sex offences
item.description: A former PoK minister faces child sex offense allegations from the 1990s. He was arrested in the UK and is currently out on police bail. Ahmed allegedly failed to attend a court date, campaigning instead in Mirpur. A UK judge allowed him to travel to Pakistan despite his bail status. Greater Manchester police may seek his extradition if he fails to appear.
item.dc:creator: NAOMI CANTON

item.title: Bhawana becomes India’s 1st woman ‘Top Gun’; Capt Shivani 1st woman ADC to Army chief
item.description: Squadron Leader Bhawana Kanth became the first Indian woman to complete the elite Fighter Combat Leader course. Captain Shivani Sehrawat is now the first woman officer appointed Aide-de-Camp to the Army chief. Kanth previously qualified for daytime combat missions on a MiG-21 Bison aircraft. She later transitioned to piloting the advanced Sukhoi Su-30 MKI frontline fighter jet. These achievements highlight growing gender inclusion within India's defense forces.
item.dc:creator: SURENDRA SINGH

item.title: Iltija booked for ‘assaulting’ cop; PDP says she was manhandled
item.description: An FIR has been filed by J&K Police against Iltija Mufti, accusing her of assaulting an officer amid protests. Charges against her involve public servant assault and rioting, while her mother, Mehbooba Mufti, is also named for failing to adhere to protest regulations. The PDP refutes these claims, asserting police brutality led to Iltija's injuries and criticizing the questioning of an individual in medical care.
item.dc:creator: NASEER GANAI
